steps.title: Set up fly cross and agar plates
steps.instruction: Cross M6‑gapGFP, Duf‑Gal4 and UAS‑mCD8‑mCherry flies using 40–60 adults in an embryo‑collection cage; prepare apple/grape juice agar medium with methyl 4‑hydroxybenzoate, pour into 35 mm cell‑culture dishes, let solidify at room temperature and store plates at 4 °C (up to 2 weeks).

steps.title: Collect and age‑synchronize embryos
steps.instruction: Add a central yeast paste layer to each agar plate, place the plates in the cage and incubate flies at 25 °C with a 12:12 h light/dark cycle for two days; change plates every 12 h (or transfer flies to a new cage every 2 h) to obtain embryos aged 0–12 h.

steps.title: Wash embryos into dechorionation chamber
steps.instruction: Using a fine brush, wash embryos from the plates into a dechorionation chamber and rinse repeatedly with water to remove all yeast paste.

steps.title: Dechorionate embryos with bleach
steps.instruction: Swirl the embryos in 50 % commercial bleach (4 % available chlorine) for up to 2 min until they appear as shiny rice granules; confirm chorion removal under a dissection microscope.

steps.title: Rinse and pat‑dry embryos
steps.instruction: Thoroughly rinse the dechorionated embryos with distilled water, then place the nylon mesh on a pile of Kleenex tissues and pat dry for a few minutes; after 2–3 min of drying, pick embryo clusters with a fine brush or dissecting needle.

steps.title: Transfer embryos to agar block
steps.instruction: Place the picked embryo clusters onto a rectangular block of apple juice agar cut from the square cell‑culture plates that contains a uniform agar layer.

steps.title: Align embryos on agar block
steps.instruction: Arrange the embryos in a linear fashion along the edge of the agar block so that the dorsal side faces the edge and the lateral side faces upward for optimal visualization of abdominal AMPs.

steps.title: Prepare heptane glue solution
steps.instruction: In a 100 mL glass bottle, lay approximately ten 10 × 1 cm strips of double‑sided tape, add 90 mL N‑heptane, and let the mixture sit at room temperature for 12 h; the heptane‑glue solution can be stored at 4 °C for future use.

steps.title: Apply glue to coverslip
steps.instruction: Using a P10 micropipette, dispense a small volume of the heptane‑glue solution as a thin line across the center of a rectangular coverslip, covering its entire length; allow the glue to semidry for 5 min in a sterile empty plastic box.

steps.title: Transfer embryos onto coverslip
steps.instruction: Gently press the glue‑coated side of the coverslip against the aligned embryos on the agar block, transferring them to the coverslip with the same orientation (lateral side facing the coverslip).

steps.title: Cover embryos with halocarbon oil
steps.instruction: Add a thin layer of Halocarbon oil 27 over the embryos to prevent desiccation while allowing gas exchange.

steps.title: Image embryos by confocal microscopy
steps.instruction: Place the prepared coverslip in an inverted microscope using appropriate holders; on a Leica SP5 confocal set to time‑series mode, select suitable embryos, use a 40× oil‑immersion objective, acquire Z‑stacks and time‑lapse series as needed.

substeps.instruction: Mount coverslip as for a glass slide.
Select embryos of the desired developmental stage.
Use 40× oil immersion objective for high‑resolution imaging.
Collect Z‑stacks covering the tissue depth of interest.
Record time‑lapse series for live imaging.

steps.title: Process images for analysis
steps.instruction: Import raw confocal files into Fiji (ImageJ) to generate Z‑stack images, then use Imaris (BitPlane) for 3‑D reconstruction of single‑time‑point and time‑series datasets.
